39:# Security overrides for transitive deps that parents pin to vulnerable versions
40-# (Dependabot can't auto-PR these — they're not in any manifest). Selectors only
41-# touch the vulnerable range, so a patched parent later resolves normally.
42-#
43-# Selectors are bounded on BOTH ends and the replacement is capped to the selector's
44-# own major, so a consumer of some other major is never silently dragged across a
45-# major boundary. The one deliberate exception is brace-expansion 4.x (see below).
46:overrides:
47-  # GHSA-3jxr-9vmj-r5cp / GHSA-mh99-v99m-4gvg / GHSA-rgw5-rvv9-x895 — brace-expansion ReDoS.
48-  # Two majors are in the graph (1.x under minimatch@3, 5.x under minimatch@10), so each
49-  # line needs its own floor.
50-  'brace-expansion@>=1.0.0 <1.1.18': '>=1.1.18 <2'
51-  # Deliberate cross-major rewrite, and the only one in this block. The advisories model
52-  # 4.x and 5.x as a single vulnerable range fixed in 5.0.9: upstream published just 4.0.0
53-  # and 4.0.1, never backported the fix, and ships no maintenance-v4 tag — so no secure
54-  # 4.x target exists. 5.0.9 requires node "20 || >=22", which this workspace satisfies
55-  # (every package declares engines.node >=24, enforced by engineStrict above, and
56-  # .prototools pins 24.16.0). Nothing resolves to 4.x today; this
57-  # selector exists so a future 4.x consumer is migrated rather than left unpatched.
58-  'brace-expansion@>=4.0.0 <5.0.9': '>=5.0.9 <6'
59-  # GHSA-73wf-gq98-2v4g / GHSA-c83g-rgw3-j3cx — browserslist. normalizeStats() walks an
60-  # untrusted browserslist-stats.json with an unguarded for...in, so an inherited
61-  # Object.prototype key (e.g. "toString") crashes it and a literal "__proto__" key reaches
62-  # the real prototype setter; separately its two result caches never evict. Reaches the
63-  # graph only through @babel/core (styled-jsx -> next, and eslint-plugin-react-hooks).
64-  'browserslist@>=4.0.0 <4.28.7': '>=4.28.7 <5'
65-  # fast-uri. Transitive via ajv@8. Three waves of advisories, so the floor has moved three times:
66-  # GHSA-v2hh-gcrm-f6hx / GHSA-7p8r-x3mc-p8w7 were fixed in 3.1.5, and GHSA-5jgf-p345-68v8 /
67-  # GHSA-f65p-4m7j-42xc / GHSA-fph4-wmhf-6fwf / GHSA-jqff-g426-hqxp then landed AGAINST 3.1.5
68-  # itself — host confusion via skipped IDN canonicalization and via percent-encoded scheme
69-  # normalization, plus SSRF via malformed IPv6 normalization and via repeated hostname
70-  # percent-decoding. All four are fixed in 3.1.6 on the 3.x line (upstream also shipped 2.4.5
71-  # and 4.1.3 for the other two majors; only 3.x is in this graph). The third wave,
72-  # GHSA-333x-w4r6-6crp / GHSA-w74x-v6f9-j3xg / GHSA-wjr9-j795-jxcr / GHSA-xhq7-xmqj-769h,
73-  # landed against 3.1.8 and is fixed in 3.1.9.

75-  # GHSA-3g3m-2fjr-6pw4 (CVE-2026-118773) — glob: an AbortSignal cancellation bypass lets a
76-  # traversal continue after the timeout. Vulnerable >= 9.0.0, <= 14.0.1; fixed in 14.0.2, and
77-  # no 10.x release carries the fix. Reaches the graph only through archiver-utils (archiver ->

  - The final image contents were not verified by building the image.
  - The version of Next's vendored picomatch is unknown. If a patched picomatch is released, a Next upgrade would be needed to update that copy.

# osv-scanner waivers for the npm + Python lockfiles (SMA-518).
#
# This is the JS/Python counterpart to the `[advisories] ignore` list in rs/deny.toml, and
# it is held to the same standard: an entry must explain why the vulnerable code path is
# unreachable in this repo, or why no upgrade exists — not merely that the finding is
# inconvenient. `rs/deny.toml`'s RUSTSEC-2023-0071 entry is the model. An unjustified
# waiver is worse than the alert backlog it replaces, because it is invisible.
#
# Prefer fixing over waiving. For a pinned npm transitive, add a range-scoped selector to
# the `overrides:` block in ts/pnpm-workspace.yaml; for Python, the package manager lock upgrade of one package.
#
# Format (osv-scanner 2.x):
#
#   [[IgnoredVulns]]
#   id = "GHSA-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx"
#   # ignoreUntil = 2026-01-01   # optional — the waiver re-fires after this date
#   reason = "Why the vulnerable path is unreachable here, or why no fix exists."
#
# When a waiver's reason depends on "no shipped package reaches it", the advisory must also
# be in SHIPPED_FREE_WAIVERS in ci/osv/shipped_reachability.py. ci/osv/run.sh runs that
# guard, and it fails when a shipped importer reaches the waived package.
#
# The first waiver is GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm (braces, SMA-733). Every earlier finding was
# fixed by upgrading.

# GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm (CVE-2026-93687, severity 8.7): "braces vulnerable to
# stack-exhaustion denial of service through deeply nested patterns". It affects
# braces@3.0.3 in ts/pnpm-lock.yaml.
#
# No fix: osv.dev records introduced=0, last_affected=3.0.3, and 3.0.3 is the newest braces
# on npm. No upgrade removes the path: the newest micromatch (4.0.8), fast-glob (3.3.3),
# @next/eslint-plugin-next (16.3.8, which pins fast-glob 3.3.1), semantic-release (25.0.9)
# and @semantic-release/commit-analyzer (13.0.1) all still reach braces.
#
# Who reaches it: only micromatch@4.0.8, and only from the root importer `.` through
# devDependencies (@next/eslint-plugin-next -> fast-glob, semantic-release,
# @semantic-release/commit-analyzer). No console image contains it: ts/Dockerfile installs
# with --filter "@paigasus/${APP}...", which excludes the root importer, and the image ships
# only .next/standalone and .next/static.
#
# Threat model: micromatch calls braces only to expand a glob pattern, and fast-glob expands
# only the patterns it gets. These tools expand only patterns that the repo's own config
# holds (for example the ESLint config's settings.next.rootDir). A fork PR can change those
# patterns. The worst result is then a stack exhaustion that stops that PR's own CI job,
# which has no write credentials. No workflow runs semantic-release, so no release job runs
# braces on untrusted input.
#
# Guard: ci/osv/shipped_reachability.py fails `repo:osv` when a shipped importer (apps/* and
# the workspace packages they link) reaches braces. Residual: nothing reds if someone
# deletes the guard call from ci/osv/run.sh (SMA-733 spec section 4.5).
[[IgnoredVulns]]
id = "GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm"
ignoreUntil = 2027-01-02
reason = "No fixed braces release. Only root dev tooling (ESLint Next plugin, semantic-release) reaches it, on repo-authored glob patterns; no shipped package does, and ci/osv/shipped_reachability.py enforces that (SMA-733)."
---
