python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
p = Path("osv-scanner.toml")
t = p.read_text()
old = "# The first waiver is GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm (braces, SMA-733). Every earlier finding was\n# fixed by upgrading.\n"
new = ("# The first waiver is GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm (braces, SMA-733). Every earlier finding was\n"
       "# fixed by upgrading. The second is GHSA-fc5q-39xc-vjpf (picomatch, SMA-778). It is NOT in\n"
       "# SHIPPED_FREE_WAIVERS, because app devDependencies reach it; its comment says why.\n")
assert t.count(old) == 1
t = t.replace(old, new)
t = t.rstrip("\n") + "\n" + '''
# GHSA-fc5q-39xc-vjpf (CVE-2026-112366, severity 8.7): "picomatch vulnerable to ReDoS
# through single-branch repeated extglobs". It affects picomatch@2.3.2 and picomatch@4.0.7
# in ts/pnpm-lock.yaml. An attacker must control the GLOB PATTERN, for example `+(*)`.
#
# No fix: the GitHub advisory lists no patched version for <= 4.0.7, and 4.0.7 is the newest
# picomatch on npm (checked 2026-11-17). No pnpm override can raise it.
#
# Who reaches it: only devDependencies and root tooling. picomatch@4.0.7 comes through
# vitest, vite (fdir, tinyglobby), msw, typescript-eslint and semantic-release.
# picomatch@2.3.2 comes only through micromatch@4.0.8 under root devDependencies.
# No app production dependency reaches either version.
#
# Why this waiver is NOT in SHIPPED_FREE_WAIVERS: ci/osv/shipped_reachability.py counts app
# devDependencies as shipped, and apps/gateway-console > vitest > picomatch@4.0.7 makes it
# exit 3. The guard is right that ts/Dockerfile installs those devDependencies in the BUILDER
# stage. The final distroless stage copies only /app, which holds the Next.js standalone
# output (an nft trace of the files that app code requires). Nothing measured the final image
# contents for this waiver; that fact comes from ts/Dockerfile.
#
# Threat model: no source file in ts/apps or ts/packages imports picomatch, micromatch,
# tinyglobby, fast-glob or minimatch. The test and build tools match only repo-authored
# patterns. Next.js ships its own vendored picomatch (next/dist/compiled/picomatch, version
# unknown). At runtime it compiles only images.remotePatterns and images.localPatterns from
# next.config, and this repo sets neither. A request controls only the string that is
# matched, never the pattern.
#
# Residual: nothing reds if an app later passes an untrusted pattern to a glob library, or
# adds a production dependency that does. The short ignoreUntil makes someone re-check this
# within 30 days. When upstream ships a fix, delete this waiver and add a range-scoped
# override in ts/pnpm-workspace.yaml (SMA-778).
[[IgnoredVulns]]
id = "GHSA-fc5q-39xc-vjpf"
ignoreUntil = 2026-12-17
reason = "No fixed picomatch release. Only devDependencies and root tooling (vitest, vite, msw, ESLint, semantic-release) reach it, on repo-authored patterns; the final image copies only the Next standalone output, and no runtime code passes an untrusted glob pattern (SMA-778)."
'''
p.write_text(t)
PY
git diff --stat; export PATH="$HOME/.proto/shims:$HOME/.proto/bin:$PATH" PROTO_REPORTER=text; bash ci/osv/run.sh; echo "rc=$?"

I checked the failed security scan and prepared a fix. PR 486 is green, and it waits for your approval to merge.

**What failed:** only the scheduled `security-scan` run on `main` today (run 44131315368). Its job `osv advisory scan` found a new advisory, GHSA-fc5q-39xc-vjpf (CVE-2026-112366, high). It affects `picomatch` 2.3.2 and 4.0.7. It is a ReDoS attack, and the attacker must control the glob pattern. The earlier failures on 6 and 7 November were already fixed.

**Why a waiver:**
- No fixed release exists. 4.0.7 is the newest `picomatch` on npm, so a pnpm override cannot help.
- `picomatch` comes only through devDependencies and root tooling: `vitest`, `vite`, `msw`, ESLint and `semantic-release`. They match only patterns from the repo.
- The final image copies only the Next.js `standalone` output. This comes from `ts/Dockerfile`; I did not build the image to verify it.
- Next.js has its own copy of `picomatch`. That copy runs only for `images.remotePatterns` and `images.localPatterns`, and our config sets neither. Its version is unknown.

**The fix:** you chose the short plain waiver.
- **Linear:** SMA-778, with project, milestone, priority and labels set.
- **Change:** `osv-scanner.toml` gets an `[[IgnoredVulns]]` entry with `ignoreUntil = 2026-12-17` and a full comment. The comment states the facts, the residual risk, and why the waiver is not in `SHIPPED_FREE_WAIVERS`.
- **PR 486:** https://github.com/SMK1085/paigasus-core/pull/486
- **Checks:** `ci/osv/run.sh` passed locally with rc 0. On the PR, all checks passed (`moon ci`, `osv advisory scan`, CodeRabbit), and the state is `CLEAN`. CodeRabbit left no review comments.

**A gap that stays open:** no check fails if an app later gives an untrusted pattern to a glob library. The guard does not cover this waiver. The waiver expires on 2026-12-17, and then the scan goes red again, so someone must check this again.

**1Password is still locked.** The SSH agent cannot sign, so I made the commit through the GitHub Contents API. GitHub reports the commit as `verified: false`. A squash merge replaces it with a new commit. Please unlock 1Password before you push or commit in this checkout.

lines: # guard, and it fails when a shipped importer reaches the waived package.
# The first waiver is GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm (braces, SMA-733). Every earlier finding was
-# fixed by upgrading.
+# fixed by upgrading. The second is GHSA-fc5q-39xc-vjpf (picomatch, SMA-778). It is NOT in
+# SHIPPED_FREE_WAIVERS, because app devDependencies reach it; its comment says why.
# GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm (CVE-2026-93687, severity 8.7): "braces vulnerable to
# stack-exhaustion denial of service through deeply nested patterns". It affects
id = "GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm"
ignoreUntil = 2027-01-02

reason = "No fixed braces release. Only root dev tooling (ESLint Next plugin, semantic-release) reaches it, on repo-authored glob patterns; no shipped package does, and ci/osv/shipped_reachability.py enforces that (SMA-733)."
+# GHSA-fc5q-39xc-vjpf (CVE-2026-112366, severity 8.7): "picomatch vulnerable to ReDoS
+# through single-branch repeated extglobs". It affects picomatch@2.3.2 and picomatch@4.0.7
+# in ts/pnpm-lock.yaml. An attacker must control the GLOB PATTERN, for example `+(*)`.
+# No fix: the GitHub advisory lists no patched version for <= 4.0.7, and 4.0.7 is the newest
+# picomatch on npm (checked 2026-11-17). No pnpm override can raise it.
+# Who reaches it: only devDependencies and root tooling. picomatch@4.0.7 comes through
+# vitest, vite (fdir, tinyglobby), msw, typescript-eslint and semantic-release.
+# picomatch@2.3.2 comes only through micromatch@4.0.8 under root devDependencies.
+# No app production dependency reaches either version.
+# Why this waiver is NOT in SHIPPED_FREE_WAIVERS: ci/osv/shipped_reachability.py counts app
+# devDependencies as shipped, and apps/gateway-console > vitest > picomatch@4.0.7 makes it
+# exit 3. The guard is right that ts/Dockerfile installs those devDependencies in the BUILDER
+# stage. The final distroless stage copies only /app, which holds the Next.js standalone
+# output (an nft trace of the files that app code requires). Nothing measured the final image
+# contents for this waiver; that fact comes from ts/Dockerfile.
+# Threat model: no source file in ts/apps or ts/packages imports picomatch, micromatch,
+# tinyglobby, fast-glob or minimatch. The test and build tools match only repo-authored
+# patterns. Next.js ships its own vendored picomatch (next/dist/compiled/picomatch, version
+# unknown). At runtime it compiles only images.remotePatterns and images.localPatterns from
+# next.config, and this repo sets neither. A request controls only the string that is
+# matched, never the pattern.
+# Residual: nothing reds if an app later passes an untrusted pattern to a glob library, or
+# adds a production dependency that does. The short ignoreUntil makes someone re-check this
+# within 30 days. When upstream ships a fix, delete this waiver and add a range-scoped
+# override in ts/pnpm-workspace.yaml (SMA-778).
+[[IgnoredVulns]]
+id = "GHSA-fc5q-39xc-vjpf"
+ignoreUntil = 2026-12-17

+reason = "No fixed picomatch release. Only devDependencies and root tooling (vitest, vite, msw, ESLint, semantic-release) reach it, on repo-authored patterns; the final image copies only the Next standalone output, and no runtime code passes an untrusted glob pattern (SMA-778)."
